The original row crosses state, HTTP authority, daemon entry, launcher, and browser UI; a single plan would exceed the 5-file review bar and would collide with unresolved dirty launcher paths. Authority model: the browser receives a non-authoritative confirmation label and request id in response bodies only. A racing loopback client may request but cannot approve. The local operator sees the browser label and enters it at `moe up`; the launcher uses its already-resolved, never-printed MOE_DAEMON_CREDENTIAL to call the authenticated approve route. Only that approved matching request can claim one session. The label alone never grants authority and is not a substitute bearer.
